what_happened: While reading request 20261015-215703-px13, the reader (Athena's reading step) stopped at reading 1 and asked the user a question. It assumed that only invocations/01-reader.json from job 2fsa is committed, and that the producer invocation record exists only in the state directory. Neither the repository nor the defaults could confirm this. The user answered that the assumption holds. The event was logged as a correction, but it was an answered question: the user did not fix a wrong reading.
cause: The reader works from the repository, but some of an earlier job's records exist only in the state directory outside it. Nothing gives the reader an inventory of what is committed and what is state-only for a referenced job. The reader can't check its own assumption about this, so a person has to confirm it. The earlier cases in class 85d6 are about how to verify quality. This case is about a fact the reader can't observe, so it does not belong there.
prevention: Before the reading step runs on a request that references an earlier job, Athena should generate a manifest for that job. It lists each invocation record and says whether it is committed in the repo or only in the state directory. It should give the manifest to the reader as input. The reader can then settle the assumption itself and only ask when the manifest has no entry. A code check should also flag any reader question that the manifest could have answered.
proposed_request: When a request references an earlier job, Athena should build a manifest of that job's artifacts before reading starts. For each invocation record, such as invocations/01-reader.json, the manifest should say whether it is committed in the repository or exists only in the state directory. It should pass the manifest to the reader as input. The reader should use the manifest to settle questions about which sources exist and should ask the user only when the manifest has no entry. Show this works on job 2fsa: the reader should find that only 01-reader.json is committed and the producer record is state-only, without asking the user.
